content: Have you ever wondered why we can't see the tiny things that make us sick? One day, Rohan ate a shiny red apple without washing his hands. The next morning, his tummy hurt a lot! But the apple looked perfectly clean! What was hiding on it?
Why do you think Rohan fell sick even though the apple looked clean? Could there be invisible monsters living on our hands right now?
Ask students to look at their hands closely. Ask them if their hands are 'really' clean. This builds curiosity and encourages them to make guesses without fear of being wrong.

content.title: The Invisible Monsters
content.description: Just like tiny dust particles float in the air, invisible monsters called germs live on surfaces. When we touch things, they jump onto our hands!

content: These invisible monsters are actually called Germs (कीटाणु). They are so small that we cannot see them with our eyes, but they can make us ill if they go inside our body.

definition: Very tiny living things that can cause sickness. We need a microscope to see them.

question: What are the tiny invisible things on unwashed hands that can make us sick?

content: Think about everything you touched today since you woke up. Your shoes, your toys, the doorknob, maybe a pet? If you were a germ, where would you hide the most?
Because germs are everywhere, washing our hands with soap is just like putting up a superhero shield! It washes away the germs and keeps our body safe and running smoothly.
The 20-Second Rule! Next time you wash your hands, sing the 'Happy Birthday' song twice. That's exactly how long it takes for the soap to defeat all the germs on your hands! Try it today.
Imagine your body is a super-fast sports car. If you fill a race car with muddy water instead of petrol, will it win the race? Of course not!
What happens to your body when you only eat chips, chocolates, and cold drinks every day instead of fresh vegetables? Does your body get the right fuel to run?

content.title: Fueling the Human Car
content.description: Healthy food is like premium fuel for your body. It gives you energy to play, helps you grow taller, and makes your brain sharper!

content: Foods that make us strong and give us energy are called Healthy Foods (स्वस्थ भोजन). Foods that taste good but don't help us grow are called Junk Foods (जंक फूड).

definition: Food that provides our body with energy and helps us grow, like fruits, vegetables, milk, and pulses.

question: Which of these is the BEST fuel to make your body grow strong?
options: A glass of milk and an apple

content: Many students think fruit juice from a packet is very healthy. Remind them that fresh, whole fruits are much better because packaged juices have a lot of added sugar!
Explain it to your friend: If you want to become a strong superhero or the fastest runner in your school, what should you eat for breakfast tomorrow?
Just like a small plant needs good soil, water, and sunlight to grow into a big tree, our bodies need healthy food and clean water. Without them, both plants and humans would become weak!

The Plate Challenge: Draw a big circle on a piece of paper for a plate. Draw your favorite healthy food on one side and your favorite junk food on the other. Try to eat from the healthy side every day!
